title: U.S. House · Texas's 4th District
area: Northeast Texas, including part of Collin County and areas toward the Oklahoma and Arkansas borders

context.text: Incumbent Pat Fallon (R) defeated Don Horn in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Jason Pearce defeated Andrew Rubell in the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Pat Fallon

summary.text: Pat Fallon is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 4th Congressional District. A former Air Force officer and business owner, he served on the Frisco city council and in both chambers of the Texas Legislature before his election to Congress, where he sits on the Armed Services, Intelligence and Oversight committees and chairs the Military Personnel subcommittee.

background.text: Earned a degree in government and international relations from the University of Notre Dame in 1990. His official biography says he played varsity football under coach Lou Holtz and was a member of the 1988 national championship team.

Received a commission as an Air Force officer upon graduation and, according to his official biography, was stationed at Sheppard Air Force Base in Wichita Falls, Texas. He served on active duty for four years and received an honorable discharge at the rank of captain.
Worked as an entrepreneur and as president and CEO of Virtus Apparel; his official biography says he founded more than a dozen companies.
Served on the Frisco city council from 2009 to 2012, including as mayor pro tem from 2011 to 2012.
Served in the Texas House of Representatives (District 106) from 2013 to 2019 and in the Texas Senate (District 30) from 2019 to 2021.

Has represented Texas's 4th Congressional District since 2021, succeeding John Ratcliffe. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Armed Services Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Military Personnel, the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and the Oversight Committee.

According to his official biography, he completed the World Marathon Challenge (seven marathons on seven continents in seven days) on January 29, 2016, to raise funds and awareness for pediatric cancer research.

record.text: Serves on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (including the Delivering on Government Efficiency Subcommittee) and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in the 2025–2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Jason Pearce
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary against Andrew Rubell, 52.0% to 48.0%

summary.text: Jason Pearce is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 4th Congressional District and a first-time candidate from Plano. He has worked in sales, customer service and mortgage lending, among other jobs, and describes his campaign as focused on getting money out of politics, term limits and affordability.

background.text: Born and raised in Plano, Texas, in 1993; graduated from Plano Senior High School.

Has worked in sales, customer service, mortgage loan origination, and as a chef, restaurant manager, sales trainer, day trader, security manager and insurance advisor. In his Ballotpedia survey he says he worked 14 years in sales and customer service and was a mortgage loan originator from 2019 to 2021.

Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the district over Andrew Rubell. In his Ballotpedia survey he says he had not planned to run for office before this year; he lists term limits with mandatory retirement at 65, banning lobbying and overturning Citizens United, and barring companies from buying single-family homes as his key messages.

priorities.text: Supports term limits and mandatory retirement at age 65 for all offices, including the judiciary.
Supports banning lobbying by former members of Congress and overturning Citizens United v. FEC to reduce the role of PAC money in politics.

candidates.researchNotes: Pearce's Ballotpedia survey focuses on campaign-finance and term-limits reform rather than the guide's fixed issue list; no direct statements on the ISSUES keys were found.
